column1: Starting on main, create and switch to a new feature branch with {{c1::git checkout -b feature/add-customer-email}}.
column2:
The command creates a branch at your current commit and switches to it. Start on an up-to-date main so the branch begins with the intended schema, then make the change away from main.
Review source

column1: Push committed changes on feature/add-customer-email to origin with {{c1::git push origin feature/add-customer-email}}.
column2:
The push sends your commits to the named branch on origin. It does not merge them into main. Open a pull request so the remote changes can be reviewed.
Review source

column1: A GitHub Actions workflow for proposed database changes normally uses the {{c1::pull_request}} event.
column2:
The event runs checks on proposed changes before they are merged. Configure a job to build the SQL project so reviewers receive feedback on the proposed schema.
Review source

column1: For a GitHub Actions pull_request from feature/add-email into main, branches: [main] filters on main because it is the PR's {{c1::target branch}}.
column2:
For pull_request, branches refers to the base branch receiving the changes. A request from any feature branch into main can match. It does not filter by the feature branch's name.
Review source

column1: In Azure Repos, require a successful PR build through a {{c1::Build Validation}} branch policy.
column2:
Build Validation queues a build for proposed changes to a protected branch. Make the policy required so a failing SQL project build cannot satisfy the ordinary merge requirements.
Review source

column1: With the feature branch checked out and local main up to date, bring main into your feature branch with {{c1::git merge main}}.
column2:
Git merges the branch named in the command into the branch you have checked out. While on the feature branch, this brings changes from main into your work without updating main.
Review source

column1: In PowerShell, stage resolved conflicts in Tables\Customers.sql with {{c1::git add Tables\Customers.sql}}.
column2:
After editing the file to remove conflict markers, stage the intended definition with git add. Git records that file as resolved, but it does not check whether the SQL compiles.
Review source

column1: After all merge conflicts are resolved and staged, finish the interrupted merge with {{c1::git merge --continue}}.
column2:
The command finishes the merge once all conflicts are resolved and staged. Build the combined project to catch SQL errors that Git cannot detect before you merge the pull request.
